ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No 35), ss 5-6, 24-39 and Schedule 2 (customer due diligence, beneficial ownership identification and verification); Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), ss 18-25, 195, 200-202; Companies (Beneficial Ownership Disclosure) Amendment Act 2023 and the Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Regulations 2024; Tax Administration Act 1994; Trusts Act 2019; and the Financial Markets Authority and Department of Internal Affairs AML/CFT Supervisors' guidance on beneficial ownership and high-value goods dealers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize the certified copy before a New Zealand notary public; then submit to the Authentications Unit, Department of Internal Affairs (DIA), Wellington for a New Zealand Apostille certificate. Consular route for non-Hague destination: notarize the certified copy before a New Zealand notary public; then obtain a DIA authentication certificate (not apostille); then file for consular legalization at the consular section of the destination jurisdiction's embassy in New Zealand or its designated overseas mission. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternative paths and are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize the certificate copy and apply to the DIA Authentications Unit for an apostille. Consular route: notarize the certificate copy, obtain DIA authentication, then have the destination state's consulate legalize the document. Use one route only; do not add apostille to a consular legalization chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Pre-Incorporation and Formation Steps
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors / Incorporator of the proposed New Zealand Limited Company; company secretary notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize director signatures, then DIA apostille. Consular route: notarize director signatures, then DIA authentication, then consular legalization by the destination state. The apostille and consular legalization processes are separate alternatives and may not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitution of the New Zealand Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporator/shareholders and registered at New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize a certified copy of the constitution, then DIA apostille. Consular route: notarize certified copy, DIA authentication, then consular legalization by the destination state. Choose either apostille pathway or consular pathway, never both in a single chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a New Zealand Trading Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand licensed bank (e.g., ANZ, ASB, BNZ or Westpac) after customer due diligence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: bank officer signs the letter before a notary; notary authenticates the signature; DIA apostille. Consular route: bank officer signs before a notary; notary authenticates; DIA authentication; then destination-state consulate legalization. These two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from Register of Directors and Beneficial Owners (UBO Register Certification)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office / Registrar, supported by the company's AML/CFT compliance record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize the certified extract, then DIA apostille. incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), Part 1 ss 10-16 (registration), Part 4 ss 49-52 (issue and allotment of shares), s 152 (director residency and appointment), and Part 8 ss 189-190 (registered office requirements).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies at the New Zealand Companies Office, a division of the Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE), operating the New Zealand Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (online form submitted through the New Zealand Companies Register portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no minimum issued or paid-up capital for a limited company and no blocked escrow account requirement. The company may issue ordinary shares with no par value for any lawful consideration, including cash, property, or services, as determined by the directors under sections 49-52 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY LEGAL NAME] LIMITED (the Company) HELD ON [DATE] AT [REGISTERED OFFICE OR VIRTUAL VENUE]. PRESENT: [DIRECTOR A] and [DIRECTOR B], being all the duly appointed directors, who constituted a quorum. The Chair recorded that the Company was incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand) on [INCORPORATION DATE] with company number [NUMBER] and New Zealand Business Number [NZBN]. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT. The Directors reviewed the subscription schedule submitted by the initial shareholders and RESOLVED that the proposed issuance and allotment of [NUMBER] ordinary shares of no par value be and hereby is approved, ratified, and accepted. Each ordinary share shall carry one vote, the right to dividends as declared, and the entitlement to surplus assets on liquidation. The consideration for such shares, comprising cash or in-kind assets as recorded in the subscription schedule, was approved. The Directors are expressly authorised to file the share allotment and shareholder register entries as required by the Companies Act 1993. 2. BANK ACCOUNT AND FINANCIAL AUTHORISATION. RESOLVED that the Company opens and maintains a corporate banking account with [BANK NAME] at [BRANCH ADDRESS]. The Directors are authorised to execute the bank mandate, account opening agreements, FATCA and CRS declarations, and anti-money laundering and countering financing of terrorism due diligence certificates. The authorised signatories shall be [SIGNATORY A] and [SIGNATORY B]. In respect of any payment or directive exceeding [AMOUNT], the signature of both authorised signatories shall be required. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at [PHYSICAL STREET ADDRESS, NEW ZEALAND], and that such address be filed with the Registrar of Companies for the receipt of all statutory notices and legal process under sections 189 and 190 of the Companies Act 1993. The Directors are instructed that any change to the registered office must be filed with the Registrar within twenty working days. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED that [NAME] be and is hereby appointed as Managing Director of the Company, with delegated authority to conduct daily business affairs. RESOLVED that [NAME] be and is hereby appointed as Company Secretary to maintain statutory registers and coordinate regulatory filings. RESOLVED that [NAME] be and is hereby appointed as AML Compliance Officer for the purposes of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, subject to registration as a reporting entity if the Company's operations fall within that Act. These appointments shall take effect immediately and continue until otherwise determined by the Board. 5. GENERAL AUTHORISATION. RESOLVED that each Director and the Company Secretary be jointly and severally authorised to sign, execute, deliver, and file all agreements, certificates, applications, and other instruments necessary to give effect to these resolutions. ADOPTED AND SIGNED as a true record of the first board meeting on [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search, Availability Clearance, and Entity Data Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register online name availability search and NZBN lookup.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the New Zealand Companies Register website and perform a company name and New Zealand Business Number search for the proposed company name, including exact and similar names. Confirm that the proposed name is not identical or almost identical to an existing registered company or reserved name under the Companies Act 1993. Verify the intended business scope against ISIC 4791 and ensure that the name does not contain prohibited words, such as Bank or Trust, which would trigger additional ministerial consent. Record the search results and retain a screen print in the transaction file. If the name is available, proceed without a separate reservation because New Zealand does not maintain an indefinite name reservation mechanism; availability is finally confirmed at filing.
required_dossiers: List of intended directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is flagged as identical or confusingly similar to an existing name, select a new primary name or request written consent from the existing name holder and attach that consent to the incorporation application. If the registry issues a formal query, respond through the Companies Register online portal within the statutory response period and provide supporting documents to demonstrate distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitution, Statutory Consents, and Admissions of Shareholdings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors of the intended company and the applicant legal adviser, with eventual electronic lodgement through the Companies Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the optional constitution, if any, and ensure that it complies with the Companies Act 1993. If no constitution is adopted, the default rules of the Act will govern. Obtain signed consents to act as director from each proposed director, including confirmation of the residency requirement under section 152. Secure the consent of the registered office holder to use the proposed registered office address. Obtain certified identification and proof of residential address for each director and ultimate beneficial owner for bank anti-money laundering due diligence. Have initial shareholders sign a share subscription agreement and a written consent to become a member. All documents must be in English. Notarisation is not statutorily required for filing with the Companies Office but may be requested later by the bank or by transfer agents.
required_dossiers: Consent to use registered office address
Certified passport or driver licence for each director and shareholder
Proof of residential address for each director and shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office raises a question regarding the residence or consent of a director, submit a statutory declaration or notarially certified evidence of residential status and signed consent. If a shareholder fails to provide valid identification, delay the deemed shareholder allotment until the identification has been accepted by the relevant compliance officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment of State Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the New Zealand Companies Register and complete the online application for registration of a New Zealand limited company. Enter the company name, the constitution adoption status, the registered office address, the director details, the shareholding structure, and the intended business scope. Each director must electronically confirm their consent and state their residential address. Pay the prescribed filing fee by debit or credit card. The Companies Register will validate the application electronically, issue the Certificate of Incorporation, allocate a company number, and issue a New Zealand Business Number. Standard online incorporations are generally completed within one business day. Immediately download the Certificate of Incorporation and verify the legal name, company number, NZBN, registered office, and director data against the original application.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the automatic validation identifies inconsistent data, correct the affected fields and resubmit. If the application is formally rejected, file a fresh application with corrected dossiers and request a refund of the prior fee from the Companies Office only if the rejection was caused by registry error. If the certificate contains typographical errors, apply for a corrected certificate within five working days through the Companies Register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Governance, Banking Mandate Execution, and Tax Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, the corporate bank's AML/CFT compliance unit, and Inland Revenue, with post-filing compliance through the Companies Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene and hold the first board meeting, adopt the pro forma first board resolutions, allot shares to the initial shareholders, issue share certificates, and update the share register and director and officer registers. Open the corporate bank account by submitting the Certificate of Incorporation, the adopted constitution if any, the board resolution authorising the account, certified director identification, and the completed bank mandate. Execute the bank mandate with the appropriate signature threshold. Register the company with Inland Revenue for income tax, and register for GST if annual taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 or if voluntary registration is desired. Register as an employer for PAYE if employees are engaged. Maintain the statutory registers and minutes at the registered office or another location approved by the board.
required_dossiers: First board resolution minutes and share allotment record
Shareholder register and director and officer register
Bank account opening forms and bank mandate
AML/CFT policy and customer due diligence pack
Inland Revenue registration forms and GST/PAYE election
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines a proposed signatory or requires supplemental beneficial ownership evidence, amend the bank mandate by adopting a supplementary board resolution and provide the requested notarised identification. If Inland Revenue queries the GST registration or tax classification, provide projected revenue schedules, supplier contracts, and the company's business plan. If the Companies Register indicates missing officer or registered office data, update the online records within twenty working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. Online consignment and secondhand luxury goods retail under ISIC 4791 is not an industrial, manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation subject to an industrial licensing board. General regulatory oversight for online commerce, consumer protection, and secondhand trade rests with MBIE, the Ministry of Justice, and WorkSafe New Zealand as applicable.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable as an industrial operating permit. No ISIC 4791 manufacturing or facility-specific operating licence is mandated for pure online consignment and resale of vintage luxury goods, including where no owned physical production facility is established. If the company is later deemed to be a secondhand dealer within the Secondhand Dealers and Pawnbrokers Act 2004, a separate trade licence from the Ministry of Justice may be required before buying and selling secondhand goods; that is a sectoral trade licence and not an industrial physical operating licence.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable. No physical development, manufacturing plant, or discharge facility is proposed. For any future fit-out or warehouse activation, the relevant agencies would be the Environmental Protection Authority and the territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. Pure online retail and consignment activity with no physical manufacturing, no contaminant discharge, and no works on land does not require a full Environmental Impact Assessment or environmental registration under the Resource Management Act 1991. Any future ordinary warehouse fit-out would require building consent through the territorial authority, but would not by itself trigger a full national EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. No process wastewater, volatile organic compounds, or hazardous waste streams are generated by online luxury goods resale. If the company later establishes a physical warehouse, municipal solid waste must be handled in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008, and any refrigeration or climate-control equipment must comply with the Ozone Layer Protection Regulations 1996. No industrial discharge or emissions consent is currently required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable. No Civil Defence fire permit is required for pure online consignment and retail operations. If the company later uses premises for storage, packaging, or dispatch of luxury goods, the following clearances become mandatory: a building warrant of fitness and any fire evacuation scheme required by the Building Act 2004 and Fire and Emergency New Zealand, plus a workplace health and safety risk assessment and employee training programme under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 for WorkSafe New Zealand compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand; online electronic portal: myIR Secure Online Services at ird.govt.nz.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident company must first obtain an IRD number from the Inland Revenue Department. The application is made by lodging the standard non-resident company IRD number application with IRD, either through myIR or by postal submission accompanied by certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, company constitution, register of directors and shareholders, and proof of appointed New Zealand agent or tax representative where applicable. If the company will make taxable supplies in New Zealand exceeding the registration threshold, the same application must include GST registration; New Zealand administers GST under the same IRD number and does not issue a separate VAT identification number. For a non-resident company with no New Zealand banking presence, a New Zealand tax agent or registered agent must be engaged and confirmation of overseas address and officer details must be provided to satisfy CRS/FATCA and anti-money-laundering requirements before the IRD number is issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no general check-the-box election. A closely held New Zealand company may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) status for flow-through income tax treatment if it satisfies the owner-count and eligibility rules; however, for a limited liability company carrying on an online resale business through non-resident shareholders, the default treatment is entity-level taxation. Hybrid mismatch and base-erosion rules apply to New Zealand entities with foreign hybrid constituent parts; relevant elections and recharacterisations must be made on return disclosure schedules with IRD. Otherwise, no entity-classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (value-added consumption tax).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies (GST-exclusive consideration) supplied in New Zealand in any 12-month period; non-resident suppliers of remote services must register when the NZD 60,000 threshold is reached for supplies to New Zealand recipients, unless the supply is already zero-rated and the non-resident has no New Zealand establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: There is no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing clearance API, or anti-fraud digital stamping regime in New Zealand. New Zealand operates a voluntary e-invoicing framework based on the Peppol network, and GST-registered persons may use commercial e-invoicing platforms. Tax invoices must contain all prescribed particulars and be issued within 28 days after the supply; GST returns are filed electronically through myIR with periodic payment, and the Commissioner may require specific invoice or record formats under investigation but does not pre-approve transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of vintage luxury goods is zero-rated for GST where the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand in the ordinary course of the sale and the goods are physically removed from New Zealand before the expiry of 28 days after the time of supply. The supplier must hold contemporaneous documentary evidence that the goods were exported and that the customer received the goods outside New Zealand. Qualifying digital or remote services supplied to non-resident customers are zero-rated where the customer is outside New Zealand and the services are not supplied in connection with New Zealand land or goods in New Zealand; service-supplier evidence may include the customer's residence, IP address, billing address, payment data, and foreign contract terms. Zero-rating cannot be claimed unless the supplier is GST-registered and the evidence requirements under the GST Act 1985 are satisfied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) filed through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the international carrier
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent bank foreign exchange inward credit confirmation evidencing repatriation of the export sale proceeds to New Zealand
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Inland Revenue Commissioner may disallow zero-rating and assess GST at 15% on the full consideration if the required export evidence is missing, late, false, or fails to show physical export and foreign exchange repatriation within the statutory or repatriation window. The Tax Administration Act 1994 shortfall penalties apply: 20% for failing to take reasonable care, 40% for an abusive tax position, and 100% for evasion or fraudulent intent, plus use-of-money interest for underpaid GST. Export documentation must be retained for at least seven years. Retrospective clawbacks may also arise if goods are returned, diverted back into New Zealand, or if proceeds remain unpaid beyond the 180-day foreign exchange repatriation deadline without a valid explanation; criminal sanctions may be imposed for knowingly providing false export or repatriation documents.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully liberalised foreign exchange regime. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely convertible on both current and capital account transactions, with no general exchange control approvals, currency surrender obligations, or mandatory repatriation timelines imposed by the RBNZ. Payments and transfers for trade, services, loan repayments, dividends, and even repatriation of invested capital may proceed directly through the banking system using ordinary customer-initiated SWIFT payments. Current account transactions such as import/export settlement require no specific central bank authorisation, although banks require accurate trade documentation and AML/CFT identification of counterparties. Capital account items, including inbound direct investment to capitalise New Zealand Ltd companies, share transfers, and foreign-currency borrowing, are similarly unrestricted for most non-resident investors, subject to the Overseas Investment Act for sensitive land and fishing quotas; a standard online luxury-resale trading company is not sensitive. Profit remittance to overseas shareholders is permitted without withholding-tax clearance, but non-resident dividend withholding tax (NRWT) may be imposed at up to 30% unless reduced by an applicable double tax agreement, and the bank will request Form IR67 or a tax certificate. No export proceeds are required to be surrendered to any entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory or regulatory requirement exists in New Zealand for the surrender of export proceeds. Exporters may retain and use foreign currency receipts freely; no mandatory conversion ratio or timeline is prescribed. Any such retention must still satisfy the reporting bank's AML/CFT requirements and the company's own tax and treasury policy.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: New Zealand has no bespoke EMI licensing framework; non-bank payment providers must be registered on the Financial Service Providers Register and comply with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Offshore EMIs such as Revolut, Wise, or Airwallex can lawfully hold funds for NZ companies if they hold FSP registration and provide local settlement accounts; however, they are not registered banks and cannot offer a legally verified capital escrow account, direct RBNZ settlement, or a treasury-grade borrowing facility. Viability: Medium for low-value cross-border disbursements and operating expenses; Low as a sole treasury rail for a high-value luxury resale entity because of AML concentration risk, platform payment-rail limitations, and the need for structured documentary banking.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory rule compels directors to attend a New Zealand branch in person. Tier-1 banks accept fully remote onboarding using live video identity verification, certified copies of passports/driver licences, NZBN and Companies Office extraction, and AML electronic checks. Where the company has non-resident directors or a complex beneficial ownership chain, the bank's compliance committee may impose a video interview with the director and a separate verification of the company's statutory records. Consular proxy opening is not a recognised general path; it is permitted only when supported by an original notarised power of attorney, board resolutions, and the proxy's own identity documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk luxury goods valuation opacity causing apparent money/value transfer (transaction value materially above or below independent second-hand market benchmarks).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent industry-recognised appraisal or authentication certification per item (e.g., Entrupy, Authenticate First, or local gemological laboratory certificates), colour/quality grading reports for watches/handbags, prior auction records, insurance valuation schedules, and a signed director's valuation declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership concealed behind a non-resident corporate shareholder or trust arrangement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Companies Office current extract showing ultimate transitional shareholder chain; NZBN record; certified constitutive documents of each entity in the ownership chain; register of ultimate beneficial owners; trust deed or trust holder declarations where relevant; personal identity and proof of address for all natural-person UBOs, plus source of wealth declarations covering original capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment inbound from unrelated third-party escrow/online marketplace accounts rather than the declared shareholder or trading counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow or platform transaction statements reconciling each payment; seller and buyer contracts; Stripe/escrow settlement reports; platform abuse and anti-fraud compliance letters; explanations for any third-party payer, supported by original legal agreements and customer identification obtained by the platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/terrorist-financing screening matches or ambiguous country risk in supply chain (e.g., seller or buyer in a high-risk jurisdiction).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full-portfolio sanctions/PEP screening report from an independent provider (e.g., Dow Jones or Refinitiv); shipping and customs progression certificates; ultimate consignee/consignor declarations; and enhanced due diligence questionnaires with bank account counterparty confirmation for any high-risk jurisdiction connection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The injection must be effected by a SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own cleared bank account to the New Zealand company's Tier-1 bank account, with the remittance information stating 'Contribution to share capital' rather than a trade payment. New Zealand does not administer a numeric FX purpose-code regime; the receiving bank applies a Balance of Payments classification of 'Direct Investment Equity' for statistical reporting. A board resolution authorising the allotment, a shareholder resolution approving the capital contribution, and a Companies Office share issue filing must accompany the inward transfer. Capital verification is completed by the bank statement showing the foreign-currency receipt and NZD settlement, the updated share register, and an accountant's certificate confirming the issuance at NZ$0.01 or par value where applicable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier remittance; for high-value vintage luxury items, a Commercial Letter of Credit issued by the New Zealand bank and advised through the supplier's confirming bank provides security. Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) are acceptable for established counterparties with payside verification. All disbursements require underlying trade invoices, customs declarations, shipping proof, and any authentication documents. For NZD domestic payments use the local clearing system; for foreign-currency payments the Tier-1 bank will route via its correspondent banking network.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with a registered New Zealand bank covering foreign currency receivables and payables for up to 12 months
FX swap (foreign exchange swap) transactions for rolling short-term NZD/USD or NZD/GBP liquidity positions
Cross-currency basis swaps matching long-dated, non-speculative inventory funding requirements; approved through the bank's treasury product programme
Exchange-traded currency futures on major convertible pairs where permitted as a hedge, not for speculative retail-style trading
Non-deliverable forwards only when a counterparty jurisdiction legally restricts deliverable NZD settlement; NZD/NZD or fully convertible pairs should use deliverable contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual return under section 120 of the Companies Act 1993, including confirmation of registered office, director information, share structure and statutory register status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after the anniversary of the date of incorporation, each year; the recurring annual cycle follows the company's original incorporation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separately graduated late filing fee is prescribed; persistent non-delivery allows the Registrar to issue a 28-day notice of proposed removal for default. If the default is not remedied, the company is struck off the New Zealand register and dissolved. Directors continue to face liability for company obligations and restoration requires court order or Registrar consent plus restoration fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and directors report (mandatory for all non-exempt or medium-sized companies; full filing required for large companies and FMC reporting entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders for presentation; Registrar of Companies at the New Zealand Companies Office for electronic filing by large companies and FMC reporting entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be completed within five months after the balance date; large companies and FMC reporting entities must file the signed financial statements with the Companies Office within 20 working days after board approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors are in breach of the Companies Act 1993 and each director is liable on conviction to a fine of up to NZD 10,000 plus a daily default fine of NZD 50 for continuing non-compliance; the Registrar may issue formal compliance requests and the company may be placed under enforcement review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent statutory audit report (compulsory for large companies, FMC reporting entities, and companies in which shareholder requisition has validly demanded an audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent licensed auditor appointed by the shareholders; audited financial statements are filed electronically with the Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The licensed auditor must be engaged before the financial statements are approved; the signed audit report and audited financial statements must be filed with the Companies Office within the same 20-working-day filing window after board approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a compulsory audit invalidates the financial statement filing as non-compliant and exposes each director to the Companies Act conviction and daily default fine regime; the Registrar may reject the filing and the company may ultimately be struck off for continuing default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return, commonly the IR4 return, together with supporting tax reconciliation of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date the IR4 return and terminal tax payment are due by 7 July; provisional tax instalments commonly fall due on 28 August, 15 January and 7 May. Non-standard balance dates attract the equivalent legislated due-date rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts late filing penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994; late payment attracts an initial penalty, incremental monthly penalties up to a statutory maximum, and use-of-money interest charged by Inland Revenue on all unpaid amounts. Persistent failure can lead to prosecution, garnishee proceedings and recovery action against company assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Goods and services tax (GST) return and payment for companies registered under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; registration is mandatory where annual taxable turnover exceeds NZD 60,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Returns and payments follow the elected monthly, two-monthly or six-monthly cycle and are due by the 28th day after the end of each taxable period. For a two-monthly period aligned with a March year-end, due dates are 28 April, 28 June, 28 August, 28 October, 28 December and 28 February.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties and late payment penalties apply under the Tax Administration Act 1994; unpaid GST is a recoverable debt and Inland Revenue may issue collection notices, garnishee orders, offset refunds, and pursue enforcement against company bank accounts and assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer compliance obligations, including PAYE, employer superannuation contribution tax and fringe benefit tax, where the online luxury resale company employs staff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly PAYE returns and payments are due by the 20th day of the following month; quarterly FBT returns and payments are due by the 20th day after the end of each quarter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment triggers the same late payment penalty and use-of-money interest regime; directors can be made personally liable for unremitted PAYE under the PAYE accountability provisions of the Tax Administration Act 1994.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory register maintenance and annual confirmation of company and beneficial ownership information, including event-driven share allotment notices and director change notices
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office for filings; statutory registers maintained at the registered office or an approved alternate location for inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual return confirms current company structure within one month after the incorporation anniversary. Share allotments must be filed within 10 working days of allotment; director changes and registered office changes must be filed within 20 working days. There is no standalone 30-day UBO filing in New Zealand; AML/CFT customer due diligence records are updated whenever a material beneficial ownership change is identified.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain the prescribed registers or to deliver event-driven notices is a statutory offence under the Companies Act 1993; each offending director is liable to fines and daily default penalties, and repeated failure to maintain an accurate annual-return position may lead to administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A New Zealand company is legally compelled to have independent certified CPA audit procedures conducted by a licensed New Zealand auditor if: (a) it is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; or (b) it qualifies as a large company under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, meaning total consolidated assets exceed NZD 60,000,000; or (c) total consolidated revenue exceeds NZD 30,000,000; or (d) it is a subsidiary of an overseas company whose foreign statutory consolidation rules require audited financial statements; or (e) shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting rights have validly requisitioned an audit. New Zealand does not apply a standalone employee headcount audit trigger; the operative quantitative triggers are asset, turnover, corporate group and shareholder requisition tests.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: All New Zealand companies must prepare financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting practice as defined by the External Reporting Board. Publicly accountable and large entities apply New Zealand equivalents of IFRS, commonly referred to as NZ IFRS; other for-profit entities may apply NZ IFRS RDR or the Tier 3 and Tier 4 simplified NZ GAAP frameworks where eligible under XRB standards. The applicable framework is mandatory and cannot be replaced by a non-compliant internal accounting basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a separate annual beneficial owner return to the Companies Office. The annual return is the statutory annual confirmation of the registered company information, including directors and share structure. Changes in share allotments must be reported to the Registrar within 10 working days of allotment, while director alterations and registered-office changes must be reported within 20 working days. Beneficial ownership is governed through AML/CFT customer due diligence records under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, and those records must be updated whenever a material change in ultimate beneficial ownership is identified; records are retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book containing shareholder and director resolutions
AML/CFT beneficial ownership and due diligence records where the company is a reporting entity

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 to USD 600 per annum for an approved registered office and registered agent in New Zealand, exclusive of transaction-based Companies Office filing fees that typically range from USD 5 to USD 15 per event.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 to USD 60,000 per annum for a licensed New Zealand audit of a mid-sized online vintage luxury resale company, depending on transaction volume, inventory holding complexity, payment rail structure, platform escrow balances, group consolidation and internal control documentation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Flat corporate income tax of 28% for all resident companies; New Zealand does not maintain a territorial free-zone tax holiday, and there is no general patent box regime for ordinary trading companies. An R&D tax credit at 15% of eligible expenditure is available, and the imputation credit system avoids economic double taxation on distributed dividends, but none of these preferences is specific to online consignment or secondhand luxury resale.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited subject to minimum shareholder continuity of 49% under Income Tax Act 2007, Part I; New Zealand imposes no fixed 5-year expiry for tax loss carry-forward.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return filed electronically with Inland Revenue through myIR; schedules such as the imputation return and non-resident withholding tax records must be attached in pdf format.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed on or before 7 July of the income year following balance date; non-standard balance dates use the statutory date prescribed by Inland Revenue, normally the 7th day of the fourth month following the balance date, subject to tax-agent extension arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identity: full legal name, IRD number, NZ registered office address, address for service, tax agent code, balance date, and percentage of overseas shareholder ownership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned NZ Ltd, use the registered office in New Zealand as the address for service. Name the final offshore beneficial owner in the shareholder schedule; failure to maintain a valid New Zealand address for service results in notices being deemed issued and default assessments becoming fixed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income: online consignment sales, secondhand luxury goods resale proceeds, commissions, authentication fees, shipping surcharges, storage income, and any other assessable income derived in the income year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The NZ-resident entity must include all gross business income derived from its online marketplace activities wherever the customer or payor is located. Where the underlying sellers are foreign-connected, ensure that title passes in New Zealand or through the NZ entity so that the income is not mischaracterised as offshore service revenue; reconcile settled escrow and Stripe payment-rail balances with gross sales.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable expenses: cost of goods sold, authentication and restoration costs, commissions to consignors, credit card and payment processor fees, freight and courier costs, insurance, warehousing rent, wages, professional fees, software, depreciation, and marketing expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses incurred in deriving assessable income. Any inventory purchased from an overseas related supplier must be valued under arm's-length transfer pricing and adjusted before entry. Avoid deducting penalties, private expenses, or inflated overseas management fees; the Commissioner may disallow payments to low-tax associated persons without genuine commercial purpose.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income: gross income less allowable deductions, adjusted for inventory valuation, tax adjustments, transfer pricing corrections, and anti-avoidance reconstructions before loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-controlled NZ entity, prepare a profit reconciliation from management accounts to taxable income; adjust for any artificial allocation of profits to an offshore affiliate; ensure that consignment stock received from overseas sellers is included in closing inventory only where risk and title rest with the NZ entity; apply the ordinary meaning of derived to layaway and escrow-settled sales.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: provisional tax paid, resident withholding tax on interest and dividends received, imputation credits attached to dividends received, foreign tax credits properly available, and any tax payments made by agents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border shareholders cannot transfer their foreign tax credits to the NZ entity. The IR4 must claim only credits legally available to the company; non-resident withholding tax withheld on outbound dividends belongs to the shareholder and must never be entered as a company tax credit. Include a reconciliation of share premium and dividend imputation accounts where a non-resident dividend has been paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable or refund, terminal tax position, and imputation credit account closing balance; declaration by director that the return is true and correct.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned NZ Ltd must separately account for any non-resident withholding tax on dividends paid to offshore shareholders; attach the imputation credit account reconciliation before issuing any dividend with attached credits. The director signing the declaration is personally certifying the accuracy of all cross-border related-party positions, treaty claims, and withholding obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR4 triggers penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: an initial late filing penalty of NZD 250, with further penalties for continued non-filing and a late payment penalty currently accruing at 1% per month on unpaid tax. Inaccurate or false returns expose the company and officers to shortfall penalties of 20% for unacceptable tax positions, 40% for gross undervaluation, 100% for abusive tax avoidance, and 150% for evasion; criminal prosecution for tax evasion may bring fines up to NZD 50,000 per charge and imprisonment up to 7 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% NRWT on gross dividends paid by a New Zealand company to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced under an applicable double tax agreement; approved issuer levy does not apply to dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the NZ payer with a certificate of tax residence issued by the competent authority of the treaty country, together with a signed beneficial ownership declaration confirming no back-to-back or conduit arrangement. The New Zealand payer must retain the documentation and, if the reduced rate is allowed by Inland Revenue, file a Deferment of Tax Certificate or withhold at the treaty rate. If the documentation is not in place before the dividend is paid, the 30% statutory rate must be withheld and the non-resident must claim a refund via the applicable tax recovery procedure under Part 8 of the Tax Administration Act 1994.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT rates are 15% on cross-border interest and 15% on royalties; bilateral treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 0-10% and royalties to 5-10% depending on the jurisdiction and beneficial ownership. New Zealand's Approved Issuer Levy at 2% may replace NRWT on interest paid to non-residents by an approved issuer, but no similar substitution exists for royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 1,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions in an income year requires contemporaneous Local File and transfer pricing documentation; a Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required where the worldwide group has annual consolidated revenue above NZD 1.125 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations code for ordinary trading companies, but the Income Tax Act 2007 anti-avoidance provisions and the OECD agency-PE analysis require a New Zealand entity to perform core income-generating activities (CIGA) such as sourcing, authentication, pricing, inventory custody, risk assumption, seller onboarding, and payment settlement. A shell NZ Ltd managed entirely offshore and used only for invoicing, title routing, and DTA access will be disregarded and the profit reattributed to the non-resident principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-recording gross consignment sales from the online marketplace, matching Stripe or Escrow_Pay settlement ledgers to artificially lower amounts, creating fake authentication and restoration invoices, inflating cost of goods sold, submitting false GST input claims for non-existent secondhand luxury stock, and directing sales proceeds to an offshore bank account outside the New Zealand taxpayer's filing records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Act 1994 ss 141E and 143B: shortfall penalty equal to 150% of the evaded tax plus statutory late payment penalties; criminal fine up to NZD 50,000 per charge and imprisonment up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Limited liability is pierced where the director signs or directs the false return; the director is jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and shortfall penalties, must make civil restitution from personal assets, may face freezing orders, travel bans, and debtor blacklisting, and may be prosecuted as a party to the evasion offence with custodial imprisonment up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Double Tax Agreement and Permanent Establishment Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating NZ_LTD as a bare nominee that holds title, issues invoices, and receives platform payments while all commercial functions, inventory risk, seller relationships, pricing decisions, and cash-flow control are exercised by the offshore beneficial owner; dividends are then passed to an associate in a treaty jurisdiction solely to reduce dividend withholding tax and protect the ultimate seller's anonymity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act 2007 s BG 1 (general anti-avoidance rule): Inland Revenue may reconstruct the arrangement and disregard the New Zealand shell; transfer pricing adjustments under ss GC 1-13; an abusive tax position penalty of 100% of the tax shortfall; Companies Office strike-off or deregistration under the Companies Act 1993 for an inactive or defunct foreign-owned veneer entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute nominee resolutions, sign DTA documentation, or approve unsupported dividend declarations face personal civil liability under Companies Act 1993 ss 135 and 136 for reckless trading and incurring obligations without reasonable belief of performance; the share veil is pierced for restitution; director disqualification and travel blacklisting are available; criminal prosecution for knowingly facilitating an abusive tax avoidance arrangement can result in imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT and Payment-Rail Misuse in Luxury Resale
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Acting as a consignment and escrow intermediary that moves funds between overseas consignors and buyers using Stripe and Escrow_Pay without conducting customer due diligence, source-of-funds identification, beneficial-owner checks, or suspicious transaction reporting; deliberately structuring withdrawals below reporting thresholds; using layered trust and private-wealth structures to hide the true sellers of vintage luxury goods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009: civil penalties up to NZD 2,000,000 for a body corporate and NZD 200,000 for each involved director or officer; criminal money-laundering liability under the Crimes Act 1961 may carry up to 7 years' imprisonment; proceeds of crime forfeiture under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009 may confiscate tainted luxury inventory, payment balances, and personal director assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who personally establishes, controls, or instructs the payment flow and conceals beneficial owners is treated as a principal money launderer; the corporate veil is pierced for civil restitution, the director may be blacklisted and disqualified from managing a company, travel restrictions may be imposed, and the director faces imprisonment up to 7 years for criminal participation in money laundering.
